## Goal

De-risk the arena's campaign integration (AH-0MV8QT7CB0060A7A) before any build work: prove the shared campaign and upgrade-choice systems can run headless under Node/vitest with the same seed derivation the game uses, and identify every impure dependency so the design uses the shared core directly or a named thin adapter — never a divergent copy.

## Headline

A short spike that instantiates/runs the modules the arena will consume — `buildSequencedLevels` (src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts, all fixed/curve/dynamic modes), `sequencer`/`defaultCandidatePool` (src/core/difficultySequencer.ts), `WaveManager` (src/waves/WaveManager.ts), `chooseOptions`/`buildChoiceCandidates` (src/powerups/choice.ts), `MineralHold` (src/core/GameState.ts hold), and the hold-full reward application path (`applyMineralChoiceReward`, src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts) — and records exactly which are headless-pure and which need an adapter (e.g. the `EffectsRegistry` the reward applyer requires).

## Context

- The eval layer (src/ai/eval/) must stay pure: no wall clock, no I/O, no Phaser import.
- Gym↔game parity (AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1): an enabled behaviour runs the same code in gym/game and in the eval arena.
- Effort-and-risk unknowns recorded on the parent: can `sequencedLevels.ts` run headless without Phaser imports? Can the reward-application path be exercised without a Phaser `EffectsRegistry`?

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1:** A vitest smoke test imports and exercises each target module without importing Phaser or a wall-clock/IO module in the eval entry path; the smoke test lives under src/ai/eval/ (e.g. a `campaignHeadless.test.ts` spike scaffold).
- **AC2:** Every impure dependency found is listed with a concrete adapter plan (thin, named, headless) or a recommendation to not model that behaviour in this item — recorded in a comment on this work item.
- **AC3:** The spike records the design decision the arena build follows: consume each shared entry point directly vs via the named adapter, with the seed derivation (createSeededRng + buildSequencedLevels {seed}) confirmed to be deterministic.
- **AC4:** The spike makes no production code changes outside src/ai/eval/ evaluation-only scaffolding; the finding is reproducible by a maintainer (commands recorded).

## Key Files

**Key Files:**
- `src/waves/sequencedLevels.ts` — campaign builder (fixed/curve/dynamic modes) to prove headless-safe
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — sequencer + candidate pool to prove headless-safe
- `src/waves/WaveManager.ts` — wave/level state machine to prove headless-safe
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — shared upgrade-choice flow to prove headless-safe
- `src/core/GameState.ts` — MineralHold (capacity/growth/overflow)
- `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` — applyMineralChoiceReward (EffectsRegistry dependency to assess)
- `src/ai/eval/campaignHeadless.test.ts` (new vitest spike scaffold) — headless-import smoke coverage
data.title: Spike: prove the shared campaign core runs headless (wave sequencer + upgrade choices)

# Produce and validate the promo, showreel and highlight clips

## Goal

Run the committed pipeline over the gathered footage to produce and validate
the actual deliverables and manifests: the ~45–60 s promo, the > 2 min
showreel, and several short highlight clips — all 960×540 WebM with the game's
SFX — accompanied by the selection and coverage manifests, and verify the
attention-grabbing pace criteria (AC1–AC4 of the parent).

**User story:** As the maintainer, I can share a compelling promo package that
opens with action and showcases weapons, pickups and enemies.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Deliverables produced.** `capture-output/` contains: the compiled
  promo WebM (~45–60 s), the showreel WebM (> 2 min), and several highlight
  clips — all at 960×540 with an audio track (VP9+Opus or VP8 fallback).
- **AC2 — Manifests produced.** The selection manifest (source WebM, series,
  mapped timestamps, motivating intensities) and the coverage manifest
  (feature → clip + timestamp ranges) accompany the deliverables; all three
  feature categories (weapons, pickups, enemies; boss when available) are
  listed.
- **AC3 — Pace verified.** The promo opens with action (no dead air in the
  first ~5 s) and cuts on peaks; verification measures the sampled non-black
  frame ratio and the average recorded intensity, and confirms they are at or
  above the documented reference band. The **reference band is documented**
  as part of this item (with the calibration basis).
- **AC4 — Per-clip intensities reported.** The manifest prints the per-clip
  recorded intensities so the pace claim is auditable.
- **AC5 — Validated.** Each deliverable passes the pipeline's validation step
  (decodable, non-trivial non-black pixels, audio present, correct resolution).

- **Covers parent AC1:** **AC1 — Deliverables at full game-native resolution.** The work produces, written under the gitignored `capture-output/` tree: (a) a single compiled promo WebM of ~45–60 s, (b) a longer showreel WebM (>2 min), and (c) several short highlight clips — all WebM (VP9+Opus or VP8 fallback) at the game's **full native 960×540 resolution** (the game renders natively at 960×540: `src/core/constants.ts`), each carrying the game's own SFX audio track.

## Key files

- `capture-output/` — gitignored deliverables + manifests
- `scripts/compile-promo.mjs` — the pipeline under test at runtime
- `docs/dev/action-intensity.md` — reference band documented here

## Implementation notes

- This is a run/verify item: the *code* is delivered by the earlier items; this
  item executes the pipeline and records the evidence (file paths, durations,
  resolution, audio verdict, non-black ratio, mean intensity).
- If footage cannot evidence a category or the pace band is not met, record the
  gap explicitly and create a follow-up item rather than weakening the ACs.

## Deliverables

- The promo, showreel and highlight clips + both manifests + a pace report
  (comment on this item).

## Dependencies

- Depends on the ffmpeg driver (C5) and the gathered footage (C6).
data.title: Produce and validate the promo, showreel and highlight clips

# Reduce full test-suite wall clock (262–415 s) — cut Phaser re-import, per-test boots, and wall-clock sleeps

**Headline:** The full suite takes 4.3–6.9 minutes of wall clock — dominated by
re-transforming an 8.8 MB non-minified Phaser ESM bundle per test file and
~89 s of literal `setTimeout(150)` boots — so the change makes deterministic
boot the harness default, removes the wall-clock sleeps, and splits the suite
into a fast `unit` project plus a heavier `integration` project.

## Problem statement

`npm test` (= `/skill:test --type full`) has grown from 92 to 270 test files
since 2026-09-26 and now takes 262–415 s on an idle-to-loaded 16-core host. The
runtime is dominated by test-environment setup rather than assertions: `import`
+ `environment` + `transform` sum to roughly 2.5× the `tests` phase, because 96
of 270 test files boot a real `Phaser.Game` and `server.deps.inline: ['phaser']`
forces Vite to transform the 8.8 MB non-minified Phaser bundle in every worker
with `isolate: true` giving each file a fresh module graph. On top of that, most
`bootScene()` call sites use a legacy real-time boot that sleeps a literal 150 ms
per boot, and 32 test files add further `setTimeout` polling. The result is a
feedback loop measured in minutes instead of seconds, with load-sensitive flakes
already filed three times.

## Users

- **Primary — developer/agent in the implementation loop:** "As a developer or
  agent, I want `/skill:test --type unit` to return in under a minute so that
  TDD iterations and the pre-`in_review` gate do not dominate wall-clock time."
- **Secondary — release/audit pipeline:** "As the audit gate, I want the full
  suite to stay the single audit-accepted evidence while completing in half the
  current time, so release gating remains trustworthy but stops costing 7
  minutes per attempt."
- **Secondary — concurrent agents on one host:** "As an agent sharing a 16-core
  host with other agents, I want the suite to stop inflating 58 % under load and
  to stop producing load-sensitive flakes."

## Existing state (measured, verified during intake)

Cached sanctioned runs in `.worklog/cache/*/{metadata.json,stdout.txt}`:

| Run | Duration | transform | setup | import | tests | environment | Exit |
|-----|----------|-----------|-------|--------|-------|-------------|------|
| ef2008a7… | 262.33 s | 138.39 | 17.05 | 962.12 | 957.89 | 547.48 | 0 |
| 983121d2… | 290.72 s | 140.61 | 23.58 | 1017.28 | 1022.41 | 621.64 | 0 |
| 2dc8bc3f… | 314.23 s | 188.97 | 22.83 | 1173.21 | 1084.62 | 708.49 | 0 |
| e3b09bd4… | 389.61 s | 166.61 | 60.33 | 1293.00 | 1234.28 | 746.14 | 1 (1 flake) |
| 717e1981… | 415.43 s | 174.88 | 53.90 | 1469.52 | 1288.82 | 921.41 | 0 |

All runs: 270 test files, 5,975 tests (23 `expected fail`). Phase figures are
summed across parallel workers, so they exceed wall clock; the ratios identify
where the time goes. **Baseline for AC3 is the median 314 s / best 262 s**.

Repo measurements taken during intake (2026-10-19):

- 270 test files: `src` 255, `scripts` 14, `vite` 1.
- 96 test files import `phaser` / `src/test/gameHarness.ts` / `bootCombat`.
- 665 `bootScene(` / `bootCombat(` call sites; only 43 pass
  `deterministicBoot: true` (46 grep hits including the harness itself).
- 32 test files contain `setTimeout` (169 call sites).
- `node_modules/.vite` holds 98 `deps_temp_*` directories totalling **141 MB**
  (`du -ch`) — evidence of repeated re-optimisation/collision.
- Real subprocess spawn sites in `scripts/`: `build-audio.test.ts` (20),
  `capture-gameplay.test.ts` (7), `audio-balance-guard.test.ts` (7),
  `setup-github-pages-environment.test.ts` (4), `recording-cli.test.ts` (4).
- `.pi/test-config.json` only sets `timeoutPerCommand`; there is **no**
  `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json`, so `--type unit` currently has
  only the convention fallback and no project-defined command profile.
- **Cross-agent host contention (root cause 5, preserved):** load average ~13 on
  16 cores with several agents running suites concurrently; each run spawns ~15
  fork workers sharing the symlinked `node_modules`. The 262 s → 415 s spread
  (~58 % inflation) tracks that load, so every timing claim must record the load
  it was measured under.

## Desired change

1. **Deterministic boot is the default.** `bootScene()` / `bootCombat()` boot
   with a fixed-delta `game.step` instead of `setTimeout(150)`; the legacy
   real-time path is deleted rather than kept as an option (removes ~89 s of
   pure sleeping and the load-sensitivity it causes).
2. **One boot per `describe`, not per test.** Heavy suites reuse a booted game
   where the scene state allows it, resetting scene state between tests.
3. **Two Vitest projects.** `unit` (`environment: 'node'`, non-Phaser files —
   roughly 174 of 270 files) for the fast loop; `integration` (happy-dom +
   Phaser, current `setup.ts`) for the heavy suite. The full run still executes
   both projects so `/skill:test --type full` keeps its audit contract.
4. **De-duplicate Phaser transform cost** in the integration project — a
   pre-bundled/optimised Phaser dep and/or `isolate: false`/`pool: 'threads'`
   experiment, measured before adoption.
5. **Remove remaining `setTimeout` polling** in tests in favour of fake timers
   and explicit `game.step` / `scene.tick(dt)`.
6. **Bound the subprocess-heavy `scripts/` tests** so they do not serialise the
   run (e.g. a separate project/group, smaller fixtures) — measured, not
   speculative.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Baseline recorded.** A documented, measured baseline of the full-suite
  wall clock and per-phase breakdown exists on this item (satisfied by the
  Existing state table above, which replaces the original 4-row table with the
  verified 5 cached runs).
- **AC2 — Fast loop is fast (REDEFINED 2026-10-20, producer decision).** The
  `unit` project is the fast TDD loop, measured by a repeatable command
  (`npx vitest run --project unit`, or `/skill:test --type unit`) with the load
  recorded: **43.5 s** at load 26.5/27.4/24.0 when the split landed, **83–101 s**
  at load 24–44 in the final validation (141 files, 2,517 tests). The former
  "≤ 60 s on an idle 16-core host" target and its idle-host re-measurement were
  **dropped by the producer (2026-10-20)**: the host is shared and an idle
  window cannot be obtained on demand, so the measured figure is reported with
  its load rather than against a wall-clock target. The selection rule for
  "non-Phaser" and the file/test counts remain recorded (C3).

  *Superseded text:* "completes in ≤ 60 s on an idle 16-core host".
- **AC3 — Full suite cost is bounded by construction (REDEFINED 2026-10-20,
  producer decision option (a)).** The original target ("≤ 50 % of the 314 s
  baseline", i.e. ≤ ~150 s) was **evaluated and is not achievable under this
  item's constraints**, so the producer redefined it: the suite must (1) contain
  **no wall-clock waiting** — deterministic boot is the default and all 133
  remaining wall-clock waits are replaced by `advanceGame`/`stepGameUntil`,
  enforced by `src/test/deterministicBootGuard.test.ts` and
  `src/test/wallClockWaitGuard.test.ts` (empty allow-list); (2) be
  **deterministic and repeatable under load** — three consecutive full runs at
  load 12.7–24.7 green, no retries, no new flakes; and (3) keep **real-binary
  work out of the default run** — the ~140 s ffmpeg promo compile is in the
  gated `e2e` type (AH-0MVFSNO0G00035AP). Measured after the work: **346.56 /
  370.75 / 408.96 s** at 280 files / 6,137 tests (load 12.7–24.7), against the
  262–415 s / median 314 s pre-epic baseline with an identical test inventory.

  *Why halving is out of reach (recorded, measured):* every authorised lever was
  used or measured negative — C4 Phaser transform de-duplication rejected
  (`isolate: false` cuts summed import 1,090 → 402 s but breaks 78 files /
  1,202 tests; `pool: 'threads'` and the optimiser variant are slower), C7
  per-describe reuse worth ~17 % of four suites' test phase, and the residual
  cost is the per-file Phaser transform/import under `isolate: true` (summed
  `import` 674–789 s per run). Any future attempt to halve the wall clock needs
  a producer-authorised scope change — the measured trade-offs of each option
  are recorded on AH-0MVGRR51H008WP2N.

  *Superseded text:* "The full suite completes in ≤ 50 % of the recorded
  baseline — targeting ≤ ~150 s (median 314 s) and ≤ 131 s against the best
  observed 262 s".
- **AC4 — Zero wall-clock boot sleeps.** No `setTimeout`-based boot delay
  remains in `src/test/gameHarness.ts`; every `bootScene()` / `bootCombat()`
  call site is deterministic, and the `deterministicBoot` option (or its
  successor flag) no longer needs to be passed. A repo-level guard test asserts
  this so the legacy path cannot return.
- **AC5 — Stable under load.** The full suite passes repeatedly, including under
  concurrent agent load, with no new load-sensitive flaky-test work items filed
  during validation (and, where practical, removing the cause of the previously
  filed flakes AH-0MUYALJ9S0002XXZ / AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK rather than retrying).
- **AC6 — Audit contract unchanged.** `/skill:test --type full` still populates
  the audit-accepted full-suite cache entry (`scope: full`, `test_type: full`,
  `exit_code: 0`) over the combined projects; `--type unit` uses an independent
  cache key and never masquerades as full-suite evidence.
- **AC7 — Testing/validation.** New and changed behaviour is covered by tests:
  the deterministic-boot guard test above, a project-membership test asserting
  every test file is selected by exactly one project (no orphaned or duplicated
  file), and the timing measurements are re-runnable from a documented command.
- **AC8 — Documentation updated.** Every affected doc/comment reflects the new
  harness contract, project split and timing expectations — at minimum the
  `src/test/gameHarness.ts` header, the `vitest.config.ts` comments, the
  deterministic-boot convention doc from AH-0MUJK70PU003VLIB, `README.md` test
  instructions, and any `docs/` page describing how to run tests. `CHANGELOG.md`
  is out of scope (managed by the ship release pipeline).
- **AC9 — Full suite green.** The full project test suite passes with the new
  configuration (build → test order preserved, no red tree).

## Constraints

- **`.pi/` is agent infrastructure — extension file explicitly approved.**
  Registering project test types (`{"types": {"unit": ["npx vitest run --project
  unit"]}}` in `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json`) touches `.pi/`,
  which agents may not edit without explicit instruction. The producer approved
  adding that file during intake (2026-10-19, see Appendix), so AC2 is verified
  via `/skill:test --type unit`. The full `--type full` path must keep working,
  and `--type unit` must use an independent cache key.
- **No test deletions or blanket skips** to reach the timing target; coverage
  for the covered modules (`test:coverage` thresholds) must not regress.
- **Gym↔game parity convention** (`AGENTS.md`) applies: harness/test changes are
  shared infrastructure, so a change must not make any gym scene diverge from
  `PlayScene`.
- **Audit gate compatibility:** `implement.py finish`, the pre-push hook and the
  audit F3 cache lookup must keep finding a full-suite evidence entry.
- **Verification runs go through the test skill** (`/skill:test`), never ad-hoc
  `vitest` invocations, except where a measurement command is explicitly part of
  a timing experiment recorded on this item.
- **Host contention:** measurements must be taken on an idle host and the load
  conditions recorded with each timing, otherwise the 58 % spread invalidates
  comparisons.
- Keep the change surgical: no product-code refactor, no unrelated test
  rewrites.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the 96 Phaser-booting files are genuinely separable from the
  non-Phaser ones by static import analysis; a file that imports `phaser`
  transitively via `src/scenes/**` may be hard to classify. Mitigation: the
  project-membership guard test (AC7) fails loudly if a file is unclassified.
- **Assumption:** `isolate: false` / a pre-bundled Phaser dep does not introduce
  cross-test state leakage. Mitigation: treat as an experiment behind a
  measurement, keep `isolate: true` if the saving is small or leaks appear.
- **Risk — shared mutable scene state:** reusing one booted game per `describe`
  can leak state between tests and create *new* flakes. Mitigation: only reuse
  where a state-reset helper exists; else keep per-test boot and rely on AC4 +
  project split for the win.
- **Risk — timing target vs. honesty:** halving wall clock on a contended 16-core
  host is load-dependent; AC3 must be measured on an idle host with the load
  recorded, and reported with the raw run(s), not just a rounded claim.
- **Risk — audit gate interference:** changing the Vitest config could break the
  audit F3 cache-miss path or the pre-push gate. Mitigation: validate with
  `implement.py finish` and a `/skill:test --type full` run before `in_review`.
- **Risk — scope creep:** pre-bundling Phaser, `isolate: false`, subprocess
  bounding and per-describe reuse are four independent experiments in one item.
  Any of them that turns out to be large should be split into a child item and
  linked, not silently absorbed.
- **Documented correction:** the original description states the 98
  `deps_temp_*` directories total ~854 MB; `du -ch` measures **141 MB**. The
  count (98) is correct; the size figure is corrected here and does not affect
  the diagnosis.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `vitest.config.ts` — split into `unit` + `integration` projects; per-project
  `environment`, `include`, `deps.inline` and pool/isolate settings.
- `src/test/gameHarness.ts` — delete `bootDelay()`/`setTimeout(150)`, make
  `bootDeterministic` the only path, drop or flip the `deterministicBoot` option.
- `src/test/setup.ts` — DOM/canvas stubs move behind the `integration` project
  (must stay a no-op or be excluded for `unit`).
- `package.json` — `test`, and (if approved) `test:unit` script; keep
  `npm --silent test` as the full-suite entry point.
- `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json` — *only with explicit approval*:
  registers the `unit` test type for `/skill:test --type unit`.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/**/*.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — per-describe boot reuse
  and `setTimeout` removal in the heaviest suites.
- `src/scenes/GameOverScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/MenuScene.test.ts`,
  `src/scenes/Game.test.ts` — replace 150 ms/200 ms waits with fake timers or
  `game.step`.
- `scripts/build-audio.test.ts`, `scripts/capture-gameplay.test.ts`,
  `scripts/audio-balance-guard.test.ts`, `scripts/recording-cli.test.ts`,
  `scripts/setup-github-pages-environment.test.ts` — bound subprocess cost.
- New: a project-membership + deterministic-boot guard test (name TBD under
  `src/test/`).
- `README.md` and the deterministic-boot convention doc (AH-0MUJK70PU003VLIB) —
  document the fast loop and the new harness contract.

## References

- Cache evidence: `.worklog/cache/*/{metadata.json,stdout.txt}` (five sanctioned
  full-suite runs, including the one failure above).
- Original intake seed: this item's description as authored by the producer
  (problem statement, five measured root causes, proposed approach, AC1–AC6) —
  retained above with the measurements re-verified and corrected.
- Deterministic-boot convention doc from AH-0MUJK70PU003VLIB (opt-in today; this
  item makes it the default).
- Test skill typed runs: `/home/rgardler/.pi/agent/skills/test/SKILL.md` §1a.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUYALJ9S0002XXZ** — Flaky PlayScene AC4 victory-celebration SHUTDOWN test
  under heavy load (completed): one of the schedule-sensitive symptoms this item
  removes at the root.
- **AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK** — PlayScene flaky wave-accounting kill tests (Harvester
  + Pac-Man pursuer) (completed): same class of load-sensitive flake.
- **AH-0MV53ABBU008FKE0** — Test-skill runner no-ops: no
  `.pi/test-config.json` suiteCommands for vitest (completed): the reason
  `.pi/` configuration is in scope-but-gated for AC2/AC6.
- **AH-0MUJK70PU003VLIB** — Document deterministic harness boot / tick convention
  (completed): documents the `deterministicBoot` opt-in this item inverts to the
  default; that doc needs updating.
- **AH-0MTFTIZX7005DNFW** — GymDiver AC1 wall-clock flaky under full-suite
  parallel load (completed): another instance of boot/sleep sensitivity.
- **AH-0MUGME6JP0029XE8** — Test — Run full project test suite and verify pass
  (completed): the template for the final full-suite verification.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

No interview round was required: the seed context (problem statement, measured
root causes, proposed approach and ACs) was complete enough to draft the brief,
and every remaining unknown was answerable from the repository or the cached
run evidence. Research entries recorded instead, in the same auditable form:

- **Q (self-directed): Does the measured baseline in the description match the
  cached runs?** — Answer (agent, evidence `.worklog/cache/*/stdout.txt`): the
  four tabulated runs are correct; a fifth cached run (314.23 s, exit 0) was
  missing from the table and is added. Source: `.worklog/cache/2dc8bc3f…/stdout.txt`.
- **Q: Are the call-site counts accurate?** — Answer (agent, evidence
  `grep -rn` over `src/**/*.ts`): 665 `bootScene(`/`bootCombat(` call sites with
  43 opting into `deterministicBoot: true` (description said 633 / 42); 96 test
  files touch Phaser/harness (description said 89); 32 test files contain
  `setTimeout` (169 call sites). Deltas are ordinary drift; the diagnosis is
  unchanged. Source: repo grep, 2026-10-19.
- **Q: Is the ~854 MB `deps_temp_*` figure correct?** — Answer (agent, evidence
  `du -ch node_modules/.vite/deps_temp_*`): 98 directories, **141 MB** total.
  Count correct, size overstated; corrected in the brief.
- **Q: Does `/skill:test --type unit` work today?** — Answer (agent, evidence
  `run_tests.py --help` + `.pi/test-config.json`): the type exists in the runner
  but needs a project-defined command profile; this repo has no
  `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json`, so `unit` falls back to the
  convention subset. Hence the AC2 fallback and the `.pi/` approval constraint.
  Source: `python3 $(skill_path test)/scripts/run_tests.py --help`,
  `.pi/test-config.json`.
- **Q: Does any completed item already deliver this?** — Answer (agent, evidence
  `wl search` for "test suite wall clock", "deterministic boot", "vitest project
  split", "flaky under load"): no duplicate. The closest completed items are the
  individual flake fixes (AH-0MUYALJ9S0002XXZ, AH-0MV1EN1NS000QLBK,
  AH-0MTFTIZX7005DNFW) and the deterministic-boot documentation
  (AH-0MUJK70PU003VLIB); none of them address wall clock, the project split or
  the per-file Phaser re-transform. Duplicate check performed — no overlapping
  completed item found.
- **Q: May implementation add `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json` to
  register the `unit` test type?** — Answer (producer, interactive reply,
  2026-10-19): **yes** — approve the extension file. Agent's recommendation
  matched (approved as the supported project-level mechanism for typed test
  runs, keeping `/skill:test --type unit` as the single sanctioned entry point).
  Consequence: AC2 is verified with `/skill:test --type unit`; the `.pi/`
  constraint above records the approval.
- **Q: Should the subprocess-heavy `scripts/` tests be bounded inside this item
  or split into a linked child?** — Answer (producer, interactive reply,
  2026-10-19): **stay in scope**. Agent's recommendation matched (keep in scope;
  split only if the measured change turns out to be large). Consequence: the
  `scripts/` tests are handled under Desired change item 6 as part of this item,
  and any split requires a new child item recorded here.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUGME6JP0029XE8** – Test — Run full project test suite and verify pass (completed)
- **AH-0MVBMRS4K000TTTP** – Parity hardening and full-suite verification (blocked)
- **AH-0MV55OC080068H03** – Full-suite verification: typecheck, tests and build (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: 0mtftizx7005dnfw, 0muyalj9s0002xxz, absorbed, ac1, ac3 (+472 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: absorbed, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+455 more)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: absorbed, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+423 more)

## Summary
implement.py drive (implement skill) repeatedly tries to 'finish' a child work item that is already in a terminal state (completed), fails every run, and loops forever without the epic advancing. The child should be treated as done, not re-driven.

## Context
Discovered while driving epic AH-0MV9DB68T002IROX (Compile an action video) via /tmp/resilient_drive.sh (discovered-from:AH-0MV9DB68T002IROX). The looping harness itself was an orphan from a dead session and has been killed; this item covers the underlying drive bug.

## Reproduction evidence
/tmp/epic_resilient_drive.log shows 29+ drive runs, every one exiting 1 with:
  'Failed to finish child AH-0MVDV4PNZ004ZWOZ', sessions_spawned: 0, failed_child: AH-0MVDV4PNZ004ZWOZ
while wl show AH-0MVDV4PNZ004ZWOZ reported status=completed, stage=in_review (already terminal). Each run also spent ~600s in phase_drive before failing.

## Expected behaviour
drive must treat children in a terminal stage (completed / in_review) as done, skip them, and continue to the next actionable child rather than failing and looping.

## Acceptance criteria
1. drive on an epic whose failed child is already completed exits without spawning a child session and does not reset the completed child's status.
2. No retry loop: parent_advanced reflects the true state (false only when real blocking work remains).
3. Regression: an epic with genuinely unfinished children still drives them in dependency order as before.

# Add a setting to change the control scheme for the player — Intake Brief

## Headline

Expose the ship's existing control schemes (`fourDirectional`, `asteroids`) as a
player-facing, persisted setting in `SettingsScene`, backed by a per-player
`controlScheme` field in `ai_hell_settings` that overrides the shared
`ship-config.csv` default. The list of choices is data-driven so future schemes
appear automatically, and the choice applies from the next run.

## Problem Statement

The player's control scheme is currently a **shared, repo-level** value
(`ShipConfig.controlScheme` in `src/data/ship-config.csv`, default
`asteroids`). Only the Player gym — and only in a dev build — can change it, and
saving writes back to the repo CSV for *everyone*. There is no in-game,
player-facing way to pick a scheme: a player who prefers direct
four-directional movement cannot switch.

## Users

- **Player who prefers four-directional movement** — wants direct WASD thrust
  instead of Asteroids turn-and-thrust, chosen in Settings and remembered.
- **Player who prefers Asteroids movement** — wants the shipped default but the
  freedom to switch, with the choice held across sessions.
- **Developer adding a future scheme** — wants a new `ControlScheme` member to
  show up in the setting without hand-editing UI code.

### User stories

- As a player, I want to choose my control scheme in the Settings screen so the
  ship handles the way I expect, without editing the repo.
- As a player, I want my chosen scheme remembered next time I launch the game
  so I do not have to re-select it every run.
- As a developer, I want the scheme list driven by the `ControlScheme` type so
  a newly added scheme is selectable without new UI wiring.

## Existing State

- `ControlScheme = 'fourDirectional' | 'asteroids'` (`src/core/configTypes.ts:348`),
  mirrored as `ControlSchemeType` in `src/utils/movementModel.ts:20`.
- `ShipConfig.controlScheme` is persisted globally in
  `src/data/ship-config.csv`; built-in default is `'asteroids'`
  (`src/core/configDefaults.ts:598`).
- `Player` applies `ship.controlScheme` at construction
  (`src/entities/Player.ts:337`) and `setConfig()` swaps scheme live
  (`src/entities/Player.ts:614`).
- Input dispatch is scheme-keyed in exactly one place:
  `mapControlInput(scheme, raw)` (`src/utils/movementModel.ts:569`), consumed by
  `CombatCoreScene._readPlayerInput` and the gyms (`GymPlayer`) — this is the
  gym↔game parity seam.
- Player-facing settings live in `src/core/settingsStore.ts` (localStorage
  `ai_hell_settings`: SFX volume/mute, key bindings, dev telemetry sharing) and
  are edited in `src/scenes/SettingsScene.ts`, reachable from `MenuScene` and
  `PauseScene`. Its Controls section renders one row per `ActionName` with
  shared binding values.
- Ship-config writes go through a dev-only CSV plugin
  (`src/core/configStore.ts:628`); production builds read the bundled CSV
  read-only.
- The GDD already states the ship "honours the player's **saved control
  scheme**" (GDD §2.2), but the only save path today is the gym/dev CSV.

## Desired Change

- Add a validated `controlScheme` field to the persisted settings record
  (`ai_hell_settings`) defaulting to today's shipped behaviour (`'asteroids'`),
  with legacy/corrupt records falling back safely. This is the **per-player
  override**; `ship-config.csv` stays the designer-owned default and is never
  written from the settings UI.
- Add a focusable **Control Scheme** row to `SettingsScene`'s Controls section
  (Left/Right cycles, pointer click activates, keyboard-navigable like the
  existing rows) driven by a single ordered list derived from the
  `ControlScheme` union.
- Resolve the **effective player scheme** through one helper with explicit
  precedence: player setting → ship config `controlScheme` → built-in default.
- Apply the resolved scheme to the player ship in `PlayScene` when the ship is
  created, so a change takes effect on the **next run / next ship spawn** and
  never mid-run; the gyms keep their own scheme toggle.
- Relabel the Controls-section movement rows for the selected scheme (Asteroids:
  **Thrust / Turn Left / Turn Right / Reverse**) while keeping one shared set of
  bindings across schemes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Setting exists and is data-driven:** SettingsScene shows a Control Scheme control whose options are derived from the `ControlScheme` union (no hard-coded per-scheme UI branch), displaying the current value.
- **AC2 — Persistence and fallback:** Changing the scheme persists it in `ai_hell_settings` and is restored on the next load; a legacy record without the field, a non-string value, or a value outside the union resolves to the default (`asteroids`). Unit-tested in `settingsStore`.
- **AC3 — Precedence:** a single resolution helper returns the stored setting when present and valid; otherwise the ship config `controlScheme`; otherwise the built-in default. Unit tests cover all three levels and the never-mutates-the-config guarantee.
- **AC4 — Applied in game at the next spawn:** `PlayScene` creates the player with the resolved scheme, verified by a scene test that a saved `fourDirectional` setting drives four-directional input (and a saved `asteroids` setting drives Asteroids input), without mutating `ship-config.csv` or the loaded ship-config object. A change made mid-run does not alter the current run's ship.
- **AC5 — Keyboard and pointer operable:** the row is reachable via the existing focus order, changeable with Left/Right and Enter/click, and the selected value is announced in the row text.
- **AC6 — Controls rows reflect the scheme:** under Asteroids the movement rows read **Thrust / Turn Left / Turn Right / Reverse** and under four-directional they read **Move Up / Move Down / Move Left / Move Right**; both schemes keep the same single binding set (no per-scheme binding storage).
- **AC7 — Parity preserved:** the gym scheme toggle still works, scheme→input mapping still lives only in `mapControlInput`, and the gym→game parity guards (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`, gym-parity docs assertion) pass.
- **AC8 — Tests:** new/updated unit and scene tests cover each of AC1–AC7 (settings round-trip/fallback, resolution helper, SettingsScene control and relabelling, `PlayScene` application).
- **AC9 — Documentation:** the GDD (§2.2 controls and §6.6 save-data `ai_hell_settings` row) — and `README.md` where it summarises controls — describe the new setting and the player-setting-over-config precedence.
- **AC10 — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- The choice is **per-player** (local to the browser/device via
  `ai_hell_settings`), not the shared designer config; `src/data/ship-config.csv`
  remains the shipped/default source and must not be written from the settings
  UI.
- No new movement physics: reuse `mapControlInput` and the existing
  `FourDirectionalInputHandler` / `AsteroidsInputHandler`.
- Settings must remain fully keyboard operable (no mouse required).
- Backwards compatible: existing `ai_hell_settings` records keep working
  without migration.
- Do not force a scheme in gyms (they are tuning tools with their own toggle).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/settingsStore.ts` — add `controlScheme` to `SettingsRecord`, a
  default, and validation/fallback in `loadSettings`.
- `src/core/settingsStore.test.ts` — round-trip plus legacy/corrupt fallback.
- `src/scenes/SettingsScene.ts` — new focusable Control Scheme row, cycle
  handling, scheme-aware row labels, `_persist()` update, accessors for tests.
- `src/scenes/SettingsScene.test.ts` — row presence, cycling through all
  schemes, persistence, relabelling.
- `src/core/config.ts` (or a small new helper module, e.g.
  `src/core/playerScheme.ts`) — single exported resolution helper with the
  documented precedence.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — resolve and apply the scheme when creating the
  player ship.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — only if a scheme-only override is needed beyond
  the existing `setScheme()`/config path.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`, `README.md` — document the setting.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Two sources of truth** (shared CSV vs per-player setting). *Mitigation:*
  explicit documented precedence, one resolution helper, settings never write
  the CSV.
- **Gym↔game parity guard.** *Mitigation:* keep scheme→input mapping solely in
  `mapControlInput`; gyms stay config/toggle-driven.
- **Binding semantics under Asteroids** (`Move Down` is reverse thrust,
  `Move Left/Right` are turn). *Mitigation:* relabel rows per scheme (AC6) while
  keeping the shared binding set.
- **Mid-run switching.** *Avoided by design:* AC4 applies the scheme at the next
  ship spawn.
- **Scope creep** — per-scheme key bindings, per-scheme tunables in Settings,
  adding a third scheme. *Out of scope;* record as linked follow-up items.
- **Assumption:** the setting is local to the device (localStorage) and the
  control lists itself from the union, not from ship config.
- **Assumption:** no telemetry/schema change is required.

## Related Work

- `AH-0MUFE1N36007X48T` — Set Asteroids as the default ship control scheme
  (completed) — establishes `asteroids` as the shipped default this setting
  must preserve.
- `AH-0MUA8BEUR006RWCI` — SettingsScene: SFX volume slider + mute toggle
  (completed) — the settings-row pattern to follow.
- `AH-0MUA8BGE0006UAU4` — SettingsScene: key-binding remapping + reset to
  defaults (completed) — Controls section and focus order.
- `AH-0MUA8BK1E001UZUC` — Apply rebindable keys to gameplay and menus
  (completed) — how persisted settings reach `PlayScene`.
- `AH-0MUA8BLMA003U18N` — MenuScene Settings button (completed) and
  `AH-0MU9LPZ0G0015292` — In-game menu (completed) — entry points.
- `AH-0MTF0EFNZ000RPVD` — Alternative player control (completed) — original
  Asteroids scheme.
- `AH-0MUII39KX007YUQ0` — Shared player-control step across all scenes
  (completed) — the single `mapControlInput` seam.
- `AH-0MUESFKCD004SI1V` — Ship config `controlScheme` does not survive a game
  server restart (completed) — why CSV writes are brittle.
- Docs: `docs/Game Design Document.md` §2.2 (controls), §6.6 (`ai_hell_settings`).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUA8BLMA003U18N** – MenuScene Settings button (completed)
- **AH-0MUFE1N36007X48T** – Set Asteroids as the default ship control scheme and accept headerless CSV seed format (completed)
- **AH-0MUCG5T7S001F9MQ** – Keep asteroids moving and collidable during the transition (Phase 2) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: add, allow, asteroids, available, change (+9 more)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: add, allow, asteroids, available, change (+9 more)
- `README.md` — matched: add, allow, asteroids, available, change (+8 more)

## Decisions (confirmed by producer)

1. **Storage & precedence** — (a) per-player `controlScheme` in
   `ai_hell_settings`, overriding the ship config for the player; the CSV stays
   the designer/shipped default.
2. **Apply timing** — (a) next run / next ship spawn; never mid-run.
3. **Controls-section semantics** — (a) relabel rows per scheme only; one shared
   binding set across schemes.

---

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 — Storage and precedence.** "Where should the player's chosen scheme be
  stored, and what overrides what? (a) New per-player `controlScheme` field in
  `ai_hell_settings` (localStorage), used by the player ship in preference to
  the ship config; `ship-config.csv` stays the designer default.
  (b) Write through to the shared `src/data/ship-config.csv` (dev builds only).
  (c) Both: local override plus an optional 'save as project default' action."
  — **Recommended:** (a). — **Answer (producer, interactive reply): (a)** —
  per-player setting overrides the config; the CSV remains the designer default.
  Source: operator reply in the intake resumption session (2026-10-21).

- **Q2 — Apply timing.** "When a player changes the scheme, when should it take
  effect? (a) On the next run / next ship spawn (the current run keeps its
  scheme, with a short 'applies next run' note). (b) Immediately, mid-run, via
  `Player.setScheme()`." — **Recommended:** (a). — **Answer (producer,
  interactive reply): (a)** — applies on the next run/ship spawn, never
  mid-run. Source: operator reply in the intake resumption session (2026-10-21).

- **Q3 — Controls-section semantics.** "In the Controls section, should the
  movement rows change with the selected scheme? (a) Relabel only: under
  Asteroids show 'Thrust / Turn Left / Turn Right / Reverse', but bindings stay
  shared across schemes. (b) Relabel and keep separate bindings per scheme.
  (c) Leave the existing labels unchanged." — **Recommended:** (a). —
  **Answer (producer, interactive reply): (a)** — relabel only; bindings remain
  shared across schemes. Source: operator reply in the intake resumption
  session (2026-10-21).

data.description:
## Goal

As a player/operator, changing the Control Scheme in Settings must actually persist. Today it silently fails once the browser's localStorage quota is full, because the dev telemetry sink fills that quota. The fix removes telemetry from localStorage entirely: the dev JSONL sink becomes an **in-memory, per-run buffer** that is uploaded straight from memory and reset at the start of each run.

## Operator report (verbatim)

> AH-0MVIMPC11001F7WU is still not working. It seems the setting is not being saved. 1) selecting settings and change to 4 directional 2) back to menu 3) open settings and the control profile is back to asteroids

Environment (operator-confirmed): `npm run dev -- --host`, playing at http://100.106.5.111:5173/. The row visibly shows Four Directional after the change, then reverts to Asteroids after re-opening Settings.

Related: discovered-from:AH-0MVIMPC11001F7WU (mid-run scheme honouring, commit 3c75eb4c) and AH-0MVI7LRCJ006Q8SA (the control-scheme setting feature).

## Root cause (confirmed from the operator's console)

```
Uncaught QuotaExceededError: Failed to execute 'setItem' on 'Storage':
Setting the value of 'ai_hell_settings' exceeded the quota.
    at saveSettings (settingsStore.ts:262)
    at SettingsScene._persist (SettingsScene.ts:745)
    at SettingsScene.setControlScheme ...
```

Measured on current `dev` (headless Chromium, normal play): ~50.8 telemetry ticks/s at ~1,267 B/tick = **~64 KB/s** written to `ai_hell_telemetry_jsonl`. The ~5 MiB per-origin quota is exhausted after **~1.4 minutes of play**. From that moment every `localStorage.setItem` throws — including `saveSettings` — so the Control Scheme (and any other setting) silently fails to persist and reverts to the last saved value.

Three defects share this cause:

1. **Settings become unsaveable** once the quota fills (the reported symptom).
2. **Silent telemetry truncation**: `recorder.deliver` counts sink-write failures (`failedBatches`) without throwing, so a long run is quietly head-truncated; any single run longer than ~65 s cannot fit in localStorage at all.
3. **Cross-run duplication in uploaded recordings**: nothing clears the sink between runs, and the run-end upload POSTs the **whole accumulated sink**. Run 2's `recordings/session-*.jsonl` therefore contains runs 1+2, run 3's all three — the recordings double-count and the automatic evaluation sees stale records.

## Approach (operator-approved rescope — supersedes the earlier "cap the sink" plan)

Telemetry must not use localStorage at all. Design:

1. **Dev JSONL sink becomes in-memory and per-run.** `createTelemetrySink`'s `jsonl` case creates a run-scoped in-memory writer (the existing `createMemoryLineWriter()` in `src/telemetry/sinks.ts` already provides the primitive) instead of `createLocalStorageLineWriter(...)`. The buffer is **reset on `startRun`**, so each run starts clean — this is the operator's "clear it at the start of the next game" and it removes both the cross-run duplication and any need for a cap/eviction policy.
2. **Upload from memory.** `uploadDevTelemetry` reads the in-memory buffer content via an injected `readSink` seam (already the shape of `DevTelemetryUploadOptions.readSink`) wired to the recorder's buffer, instead of `localStorage.getItem(...)`. Endpoint, content type, NDJSON body and the run-end fire-and-forget behaviour are unchanged, so `vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts` and the evaluation pipeline need no change.
3. **Expose the buffer to the dev CLI tooling.** The three Node scripts currently read the run via `page.evaluate(localStorage.getItem('ai_hell_telemetry_jsonl'))`. Add a dev-gated page accessor following the existing `window.__aiHellScenario` / `window.__aiHellRunState` convention — e.g. `window.__aiHellTelemetry = { read(): string }` installed by the dev-gated wiring, never written in a production bundle (same static-elimination pattern as `loadDevTelemetryUploader`). Update:
   - `scripts/record-session.mjs` (read the run out of the page),
   - `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs` (pre-clip reset + post-clip read; the pre-boot `removeItem` becomes a buffer reset/no-op),
   - `scripts/verify-dev-telemetry.mjs` (assert against the page buffer instead of the localStorage key).
   `scripts/inspect-telemetry.mjs` is file/stdin based — unaffected.
4. **Harden `saveSettings` as a cheap safety net.** Wrap the `setItem` in `src/core/settingsStore.ts` so a full or unavailable storage can never throw out of a Phaser input handler; on failure log one clear `console.warn`. This is defence in depth: with telemetry off localStorage, the settings record is the only writer left.
5. **Update the pinned contract + docs.** `src/telemetry/devUpload.test.ts` pins "sink content left intact after a successful upload"; replace that with the stronger "the dev sink never touches localStorage" (plus "a run start resets the buffer"). Update `docs/TELEMETRY.md` and `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`, which document the localStorage key.

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/telemetry/sinks.ts` — memory sink as the `jsonl` default; keep/rescope `createLocalStorageLineWriter` (it becomes unused by the runtime path; per the coding disciplines, report rather than silently delete — decide explicitly whether to keep it as exported test-covered API or remove it).
- `src/telemetry/recorder.ts` / `src/telemetry/index.ts` — buffer access + reset-on-`startRun` seam.
- `src/telemetry/devUpload.ts` — read from memory (default `readSink`).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` (or the `runTelemetry` wire-up) — install the dev-gated `window.__aiHellTelemetry` accessor.
- `src/core/settingsStore.ts` — quota-defensive `saveSettings`.
- `scripts/record-session.mjs`, `scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs`, `scripts/verify-dev-telemetry.mjs`.
- Tests: `src/telemetry/sinks.test.ts`, `devUpload.test.ts`, `recorder.test.ts`, `settingsStore` tests, plus the script tests.
- Docs: `docs/TELEMETRY.md`, `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: The dev telemetry path never reads or writes localStorage — no `setItem`/`getItem` on `ai_hell_telemetry_jsonl` from the runtime path (unit test asserts the resolved `jsonl` sink is the in-memory writer and that recording + upload complete with `localStorage` unavailable).
- AC2: Each run's uploaded body contains **only that run's** records: `startRun` resets the buffer (unit test: two sequential runs, second upload has exactly one `run_header` and no records from the first run).
- AC3: With localStorage pre-filled to overflow, changing the Control Scheme in Settings persists and reopening Settings shows the new value, with no `QuotaExceededError` in the console (browser-level check, menu and pause origins).
- AC4: A single run of arbitrary length is captured in full (no quota-based truncation); the buffer is released on run end after upload.
- AC5: `npm run record`, `npm run capture` (action-intensity series export) and `npm run verify-dev-telemetry` still work end-to-end against the new page accessor; `scripts/inspect-telemetry.mjs` behaviour unchanged.
- AC6: `saveSettings` never throws out of an input handler; a residual storage failure logs exactly one clear `console.warn`.
- AC7: Docs (`docs/TELEMETRY.md`, `docs/dev/gameplay-capture.md`) describe the in-memory per-run buffer and no longer claim a localStorage key; the dev gating of the page accessor is documented and enforced (no accessor in a production bundle).
- AC8: Full project test suite passes (`/skill:test --type full` at the dev-push gate).

## Out of scope / follow-up

- **Incremental (per-batch) upload for crash resilience**: with in-memory buffering, a page reload/crash mid-run loses the un-uploaded tail (today it survives a reload but silently stops at the quota). Streaming batches to the dev server would recover at most one batch (~1.3 s) of loss; raised as a separate discovered-from item rather than folded in here.
- **Cutting the production/player tick rate to ~4 Hz (0.25 s)**: separate decision (prefer a time-based `TICK_INTERVAL_MS` over the current per-tick probability `VITE_TELEMETRY_SAMPLE_RATE`); not required by this fix, since production telemetry is consent-gated and uses the remote sink (no localStorage).

data.description:
## Goal

Crash resilience for dev telemetry: with the dev JSONL sink moving to an in-memory per-run buffer (AH-0MVIRYGD1000JVY3), a page reload or crash mid-run loses the un-uploaded tail. Streaming telemetry batches to the dev server during the run — instead of one run-end upload — bounds that loss to at most one flushed batch (~64 records, ~1.3 s of play) and removes the page-reload regression that localStorage previously masked.

## Context

- Parent/related: discovered-from:AH-0MVIRYGD1000JVY3 (in-memory dev sink; this item is explicitly deferred there).
- Current flow: the JsonlTelemetrySink buffers records in memory, flushes batches of 64 to the sink, and the whole run is POSTed once at run end (`uploadDevTelemetry`). A crash before that POST loses the entire run's telemetry; a reload also loses the buffer entirely once it is no longer localStorage-backed.
- Dev only: the same reasoning applies to the production remote sink, which already streams batches via `HttpTelemetryTransport` (with retry/backoff), so production is not affected.

## Proposed design

- Send each flushed batch to the dev endpoint as it is produced (`POST /api/telemetry/upload`) instead of (or in addition to) the run-end upload.
- The server (`vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin.ts`) currently stores each upload as one complete `session-<stamp>.jsonl` and runs the automatic evaluation per upload; a per-batch POST would create many tiny recordings and repeated evaluations. The endpoint (or a new `part` protocol) must therefore either:
  - append JSONL records to the run's open session file keyed by a run id/seed, and evaluate once at run end, or
  - keep the run-end upload and add a lightweight "heartbeat/checkpoint" mechanism that only recovers the tail on demand.
- UX/offline: batches sent while the dev server is unreachable should stay in the memory buffer (or a bounded queue) and be retried at run end; at most one batch may be lost on a hard crash.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: A mid-run crash/reload followed by a run-end state loses no more than one flushed batch (~64 records / ~1.3 s) of telemetry; the rest is recoverable from the dev server.
- AC2: The server session file for a run contains its records exactly once (no duplication from partial + final uploads), and the automatic evaluation still runs once per run.
- AC3: Dev CLI tooling (`record-session`, `capture-gameplay`, `verify-dev-telemetry`) continues to work unchanged in behaviour.
- AC4: Full project test suite passes.

## Status

Open decision item — parked until the in-memory sink (AH-0MVIRYGD1000JVY3) lands. Do not implement concurrently with that item in the same worktree.

data.comment: Root cause confirmed from the operator console trace: QuotaExceededError on localStorage.setItem for ai_hell_settings. The dev telemetry JSONL sink (ai_hell_telemetry_jsonl) grows unbounded (per-tick sampling at rate 1, appended every run, never cleared after upload by design) until the ~5 MiB origin quota is exhausted, after which every settings save throws and the scheme silently reverts to the last saved value. Proposed fix recorded in the description: cap the sink at a 4 MiB budget with newest-lines retention (self-heals existing full storage), plus a saveSettings quota-recovery safety net with a clear console.warn. Ready for implementation.

data.author: Map
data.comment: Volume measurements (headless Chromium, current dev, normal play, dev sink): ~50.8 ticks/s, avg ~1267 bytes/tick = ~64 KB/s. The 5 MiB localStorage quota fills in ~1.4 min of continuous play — confirming the regression path. Production/player sessions are unaffected by the quota (consent-gated remote sink, disabled by default; shipped Pages build sets no VITE_TELEMETRY_* vars). Action intensity is already time-sampled internally at 10 Hz (sampleRateHz, §6.4 EMA is dt-aware), and discrete events are always recorded regardless of tick sampling, so a lower tick cadence does not bias balance metrics. Decision pending from operator: whether to also throttle tick capture for player sessions to ~4 Hz (0.25 s) via a time-based interval knob (recommended; uniform cadence) vs the existing per-tick probability VITE_TELEMETRY_SAMPLE_RATE (~0.067 at 60 fps, irregular gaps) vs keep full rate and rely on the sink cap only.

data.author: Map
data.comment: Operator question: does capping the sink lose data? Analysis: (1) Sink writes are already silently lossy today — JsonlTelemetrySink write errors are swallowed as failedBatches in recorder.deliver, so once the ~5 MiB quota is hit mid-run, every further record is dropped and the run is truncated; settings saves also fail from that moment. (2) Uploaded data is already durable server-side: uploadDevTelemetry POSTs the whole sink at run end and vite/plugins/telemetryUploadPlugin writes recordings/session-<stamp>.jsonl, then auto-evaluation writes eval-output/uploaded/<stamp>/. A newest-first cap therefore discards mostly already-persisted older runs. (3) scripts/capture-gameplay.mjs already clears the sink before each clip and record-session reads at run end, so both only need the newest run. (4) Caveat: at ~64 KB/s a 4 MiB budget holds only ~65 s, so a single long (multi-minute) run cannot fit in localStorage at all — today it is silently head-truncated; with a naive cap it would become tail-truncated. Preferred design: evict oldest whole runs at run_header boundaries keeping the newest run intact (in-run trimming only as last resort), warn + count evictions, and raise a follow-up for the real fix (incremental per-batch upload so the sink is a buffer not an archive, and/or IndexedDB as the store).
